holdings.thesis: HOLD: no longer at the stop-loss threshold -- shares rallied +7.1% on 10/1 to ~$210 on continued AI/optical-connectivity optimism (analyst consensus PT $281, Buy). Only new item is CEO William Brennan's ~$2.5M sale (10/1), continuing the same disclosed 10b5-1 program as the COO/CTO/CLO sales already flagged -- not an acceleration. Return now -22.3% vs. cost basis (was -28.0%). Position ~6.7%.

HOLD, TRIMMED for sector cap: Tech sector drifted to 30.19% of the portfolio (over the 30% sector_max_pct cap) on price moves alone. Trimmed DUOL, the largest Tech holding, back to ~29.75% -- a pure sizing rebalance. Fundamentals/thesis unchanged: DA Davidson reiterated Buy/$175 PT (9/29) citing user data; DAU growth decelerating slightly (~30% YoY vs. 34% in Q3) but still healthy; new chess course is now Duolingo's fastest-growing product line. Insider 10b5-1 sales (von Ahn, GC Chen, director Gordon) continue the known routine pattern, nothing accelerated. Position ~11.1% post-trim.

HOLD: new item -- appointed Admiral Michael Rogers (former NSA Director/Cyber Command commander) to the board (credibility-enhancing governance move). Shares +9-10% intraday 10/1 helped by a sector tailwind from Accenture's strong Q4 print. Reaffirmed 2026 revenue growth guidance of 40%+ (58% YoY reported). No new risk flags. Small ~1.8% position -- holding.

HOLD: Hagens Berman issued another 'investigating claims' alert (10/1, same Q2-miss/execution-bottleneck theory as Pomerantz/Bronstein Gewirtz) -- still pre-litigation, no complaint filed yet, though multiple firms are now circling and warrant continued monitoring. No update on the Massachusetts data-center permitting overhang. Return improved to -23.8% vs. cost basis (was -25.3%), no longer at the stop-loss threshold. No new negative catalyst found.

HOLD: mixed/slightly positive new flow -- launched Gemini 4 Argon (coding/cybersecurity model, 10/1, +2% initial) and a favorable antitrust ruling declining to force a sale of the ad exchange, partially offset by a Bloomberg report of internal skepticism on the forthcoming Gemini 4 flagship that pared gains (closed +0.5%, ~$342). Position ~14.8%, within the trim-tolerance band -- no action needed.

HOLD: AWS-demand thesis reinforced -- AWS's Matt Wood detailed ~100x AI inference cost reductions and a roadmap toward a $1T revenue pipeline, and GPT-6.1 Sol went live on Bedrock at ~1/5 the cost of prior models. New Kindle lineup launch (10/1) is low-materiality consumer hardware news. Meta 'Muse' agentic-commerce block remains in place, unchanged. Thesis intact.

HOLD: first negative rating action in a string of positive PT revisions -- Wells Fargo downgraded XOM to Equal-Weight (10/1) on relative-value rotation into BP (citing easing Qatar project disruptions), while actually maintaining its PT near $180-182. Not company-specific deterioration; broader analyst consensus remains Buy (avg PT ~$173-180). Thesis unchanged, worth noting as a watch item.

HOLD: new but minor -- announced a BNPL partnership with Crate & Barrel/CB2/Crate & Barrel Kids (9/29), rolling out in the US and Canada. Incremental positive merchant win, not thesis-moving. No earnings/legal news; next earnings still ~Nov 5, 2026.

HOLD: no material fundamental news. CEO Pomel's Rule 10b5-1 sales continue on the known routine schedule. Several analyst PT raises are circulating (Needham $300, Citi $305, Wedbush Outperform $275) from mid/late September. Thesis intact, strong performer (+23.5% vs. cost basis).

HOLD: new orforglipron ('Foundayo') post-hoc ATTAIN-1 data released 10/1 showing 45-57% reductions in predicted 10-year T2D risk and an 18% reduction in predicted CV risk at the highest dose -- an amplification of the 9/30 EASD cardiovascular-safety readout, not a distinct new catalyst. Next earnings confirmed Oct 29, 2026; NAION MDL master complaint deadline (10/28) unchanged. Reinforces thesis.

HOLD: no new company-specific item; the 9/28 Form 144 remains a routine pre-scheduled insider sale. Shares continue to trade weak (~$15.84, down 30-35% YTD) on macro/rate-sensitivity and credit-risk sentiment rather than any fresh negative catalyst. Q3 earnings call confirmed Oct 27. Core thesis unchanged.

HOLD: new item -- announced a definitive agreement to acquire Fabick Cat (a century-old independent heavy-equipment dealer across MO/IL/WI/MI), expected to close within ~30 days (announced 9/29), distinct from and additive to the already-flagged $1B North Carolina plant expansion. Commentary cites a record order book and continued data-center backup-power demand. Positive bolt-on M&A, reinforcing the AI-infrastructure-demand thesis.

HOLD: no material new catalyst in the 9/30-10/1 window specifically -- the NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center deal (9/23) and error-correction decoder coverage are recycled from the prior announcement cycle. FY26 guidance raise remains the operative thesis; position +16.9% vs. cost basis.

HOLD, continued monitoring: shares hit a fresh 52-week low (~$22.95) continuing a downtrend despite strong Q2 fundamentals (record profitability, 42% revenue growth) -- attributed to continued routine, pre-disclosed insider selling (CFO/CLO/President trimmed stakes through Aug-Sept) plus broader lending-sector/macro pressure, not a new negative catalyst. New Loop Capital initiation at Hold/$34 PT noted. AI-underwriting thesis unchanged, well short of the -25% stop-loss threshold.

HOLD: no material new company-specific news. Pentagon's newly announced 'Autonomous Warfare Command' (10/1) lifted drone-sector sentiment broadly; shares ticked up intraday then eased (~$140-143 range). Board re-elected at the 9/24 annual meeting (routine). Q1 FY27 record revenue and $1.5B backlog remain the thesis.

HOLD, continuing to flag execution/litigation risk: Pomerantz (9/29) and Bronstein Gewirtz (10/1) press releases are plaintiffs'-firm solicitation announcements for the SAME existing class action (period 3/4/25-7/15/26) already flagged, not a new filing or allegation. Board adopted a change-of-control severance plan that retail traders are reading as buyout speculation (+3-5%, no deal disclosed) -- noise. No new negative catalyst; still-small ~1.9% position.

HOLD: the Reverse Morris Trust spin-off of Modine's Performance Technologies business, combined with Gentherm, CLOSED AS PLANNED on 10/1/26 under new leadership (CEO Neil D. Brinker, CFO Michael Lucareli); continues trading as 'MOD' on NYSE. Correction to prior note: the 'Modexus Solutions' rename is NOT yet effective -- a special shareholder meeting in ~3 months will formally vote on it. Transaction executed cleanly and on schedule; small position, no action needed.

HOLD: new item -- launched the 'Dronebuster REACH' long-range counter-drone system with a first-unit contract from the Office of Naval Research (~9/30), a small positive win. Also rode the broad Pentagon 'Autonomous Warfare Command' sentiment pop on 10/1. (A widely-indexed '$425M offering' headline is a stale Oct-2025 story, not a new dilutive event beyond the 9/25 resale shelf already flagged.) Small position, no action needed.

HOLD: multiple new positives -- a 20-mission Electron launch deal with Synspective (2028-2031) makes Synspective RKLB's largest customer by mission count, pushing the total launch backlog past 100 missions; Citigroup initiated coverage at Buy/$105 PT; new $266M US Space Force multi-launch contract plus Viasat GEO-bus work; Iridium shareholders approved the RKLB acquisition (targeting close mid-2027). Shares +4-6%. Strongly positive, reinforces thesis.

HOLD, continuing to monitor closely: no negative news found explaining the 52-week-low price action ($43.08 on 9/30) -- confirms pure sentiment/technical weakness, not fundamentals. Insider Form 4 sales (CFO Lund 9/21, Carrai 9/15) are both pre-arranged 10b5-1 and predate this window, routine. Analyst sentiment actually skews positive (Canaccord PT $135 Buy, Piper Sandler upgraded to Overweight) vs. a ~$98.71 consensus PT against the ~$43-45 trading price -- a wide gap, arguably a value opportunity rather than a red flag. FY2026 guidance raise and the MACH-TB hypersonics backlog remain the thesis.

HOLD: new item -- UnitedHealthcare is eliminating prior-authorization requirements for ~1,700 medical services effective 10/1/26 (part of its prior commitment to cut prior-auth by 30% this year), a modestly positive regulatory-optics move with a minor watch-item for medical-cost-ratio impact. Q3 earnings release confirmed for Oct 13, 2026. Core thesis unchanged.

HOLD: no material negative news; reiterated plans to launch 3 satellites in October 2026 (two Mark VI with inter-satellite-link tech, one Mark V for the Sovereign Space Systems program) plus the first Merlin-constellation satellites, and a new intelligence-data partnership with SynMax. Small position, no action needed.

BUY: GE Aerospace sourced from the standard watchlist screen (quant score driven by 21.1% revenue growth, 19.4% earnings growth, forward P/E 34.4). No legal/governance overhang found -- raised full-year guidance off Q2 2026 results (adjusted revenue +24% YoY to $12.6B, EPS $2.26, record $210B backlog), engine deliveries +31% H1 2026, and a new largest-ever standalone acquisition (Consolidated Precision Products, announced early Sept) to expand engine-parts casting capacity. New commercial wins (IndiGo, United, Delta, American, Copa) and a defense-program milestone with Kratos (GEK800 turbofan test, 9/21). Passed on the higher-scoring opportunity-tier candidates on this screen -- RCAT (unresolved CRO retaliation lawsuit, insider selling and price downtrend both continuing/worsening) and SERV (FY26 guidance cut confirmed, plus a new and more severe detail: Serve says it is 'unlikely to renew' its anchor Uber Eats agreement in early 2027) -- and on HIMS (FTC suit and securities class-action both still active, lead-plaintiff deadline 11/2/26) and META (the 'Muse' rally has extended further into an unreported Q3 print, still a momentum-chasing entry). Not opportunity-tier (~$324B market cap); sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor (~$18.65), the binding constraint today, freed primarily by today's DUOL sector-cap trim.
